NOT a scriptural quotation but the common noun נבל (harp/lyre), so the MT check of step 5 is replaced by Migne's own three-language gloss in the same clause: nebel / ψαλτήριον / organum. Migne's type here shows no vowel points at this copy's resolution and none are supplied — the consonants are read, the pointing is not asserted. ⚑ The parentheses AND the trailing comma sit INSIDE the <foreign> element, which looks odd but is the source's own convention: CC encodes the Greek in this very clause as '<foreign xml:lang="greek">ψαλτήριον,</foreign>', comma included. The reason is mechanical — the chunker strips an unrecognized tag by replacing it with whitespace, so anything left outside comes through as '( נבל ) ,' with spaces Migne does not print, and a stray space before a comma is the very scar this patch exists to remove.
